findings.evidence: Line 393-394: `theorem add_landauLogScale_oneLoopCoupling ... u + landauLogScale β₀ (oneLoopCoupling β₀ a₀ u) = landauLogScale β₀ a₀`, and line 442-443 inside `landauScaleSq_oneLoopCoupling` derives `landauLogScale β₀ (oneLoopCoupling ...) = landauLogScale β₀ a₀ - Real.log (μ₁sq / μ₀sq)`, i.e. the two log-scales differ.
findings.fix: State what is proved: "Re-referencing at `t = u` shifts the Landau log-scale by `-u`, so `u + t_Λ(a(u))` and `t_Λ(a₀)` are the same point of the scale axis"; in the module docstring attribute reference-independence of the scale itself to `landauScaleSq_oneLoopCoupling` and describe `add_landauLogScale_oneLoopCoupling` as the shift law.
findings.issue: `add_landauLogScale_oneLoopCoupling`'s lead claim "**The Landau log-scale does not depend on the reference scale.**" is false as stated: the theorem is `u + landauLogScale β₀ (oneLoopCoupling β₀ a₀ u) = landauLogScale β₀ a₀`, i.e. the log-scale shifts by `-u` under re-referencing; only the point on the scale axis (and `landauScaleSq`, line 435) is invariant. Same wording at line 41-44 of the module docstring ("it does not depend on which scale is taken as the reference" said of `landauLogScale`).

findings.evidence: Lines 418-420: statement is about `Real.log (Λ² / μ₀²)`, not `Λ²` itself.
findings.fix: Reword the lead to "**The Landau scale sits at the Landau log-scale.**" (the body sentence already says this correctly).
findings.issue: `log_landauScaleSq_div`'s lead "**The Landau scale is the Landau log-scale.**" equates a squared scale `Λ²` with a value of the log variable; the theorem is `Real.log (landauScaleSq β₀ a₀ μ₀sq / μ₀sq) = landauLogScale β₀ a₀`.

summary: Module docstring and per-declaration docstrings are otherwise accurate, complete, and free of roadmap/process narrative, but two bold summary lines state equalities the theorems do not deliver: the Landau log-scale is claimed to be reference-independent when it in fact shifts, and the Landau scale is claimed to be the Landau log-scale.
